subject: QuickPulse MAP: success metrics, exit gates, acceptance tests
messages:
From: Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.inference.com>
To: Lena Ortiz <lena.ortiz@quickpulse.ai>, Samir Desai <samir@quickpulse.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.inference.com>
Date: 2026-10-21T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: QuickPulse MAP: success metrics, exit gates, acceptance tests

Lena / Samir —

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. Per our conversation, I attached a first-pass Mutual Action Plan (MAP) focused on demonstrable outcomes for the QuickPulse pilot and a companion acceptance-tests doc that outlines smoke and regression checks we recommend running during the evaluation. Attachments: QP_MAP_v1.xlsx, acceptance-tests.md (see links below).

High-level ask: agree the measurable success criteria below so we can lock the pilot scope and timeline. If you sign off, we’ll schedule the MAP kickoff and assign owners.

Proposed measurable success criteria (goal + minimum pass threshold):
- Latency (inference): P95 <= 350ms (goal); pass threshold P95 <= 450ms under pilot load.
- Throughput: sustain 30 requests/min with end-to-end average latency < 500ms during a 30-minute stress window.
- Precision / accuracy (classification use case): macro-F1 >= 0.88 (goal); >= 0.84 pass.
- Regression vs baseline: < 3% drop in critical labels during test set replay.
- False positive rate for safety triggers: <= 0.5% on sampled production-like traffic.

Exit gates (must be met to consider pilot a success):
1) All smoke tests in acceptance-tests.md pass for two consecutive daily runs.
2) No critical stability incidents during a 72-hour pilot soak.
3) Evidence of data handling & retention aligned with your security requirements (SOC2 artifacts or equivalent).
4) Mutually agreed production rollout plan documented with cost estimates.

Acceptance tests (summary):
- Synthetic throughput/stability run (owner: Redwood SE).
- Replay of 10k production-like records against pilot model (owner: QuickPulse data team).
- Label concordance test on gold set (owner: QuickPulse PM / Redwood analytics).
- Latency measurement harness with 95th/99th sampling (owner: Redwood infra).

Suggested timeline (calendar weeks):
- Week 0 (this week): MAP sign-off, kickoff meeting, assign owners.
- Week 1: Environment setup, test data handoff, baseline run.
- Week 2: Acceptance test runs, iterate on model/config.
- Week 3: Soak & stability checks, evidence collection.
- Week 4: Executive review and go/no-go decision.

Open items for your input: sample volume for replay (approx. 10k recommended), any mandatory data residency constraints, and the list of people who will sign acceptance.

Links / attachments: QP_MAP_v1.xlsx (MAP with owners/times), acceptance-tests.md (detailed test cases), SLA_draft_QP.pdf (SLA stub).

Happy to jump on a 30-minute sync tomorrow to walk through the MAP.

Thanks,
Priyom
Priyom Das
Senior AE, Redwood Inference
priypom@redwood.inference.com

Subject: Re: QuickPulse MAP: success metrics, exit gates, acceptance tests

Thanks — this looks comprehensive. A few clarifying questions before we lock sign-off: 

1) Sample size: we can provide 15k anonymized events for replay. Will that be sufficient for the label concordance test?
2) Data retention: we require configuration so that pilot data is purged after 30 days unless we opt into retention; can that be reflected in the MAP?
3) Who will be the formal acceptance signatory on our side? Procurement wants a named approver (legal/procurement will be on the contract side).

Also, can you call out which failure modes will trigger an immediate pause? For example: reproducible data leakage or any critical PII exposure.

Finally, we’ll need the SOC2 evidence before final acceptance — is that in SLA_draft_QP.pdf or separate?

Best,
Lena
VP Product, QuickPulse
Lena Ortiz <lena.ortiz@quickpulse.ai>

From: Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.inference.com>
To: Lena Ortiz <lena.ortiz@quickpulse.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.inference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.inference.com>
Date: 2026-10-21T13:40:00-07:00
Subject: Re: QuickPulse MAP: success metrics, exit gates, acceptance tests

Lena — great questions. Quick answers inline and attached a slightly expanded acceptance-tests.md with explicit owners and pass/fail criteria. (Attachment: acceptance-tests.md)

- Sample size: 15k is fine and actually helpful. We’ll use 10k for the initial concordance run and the remaining 5k for noise/edge-case replay.
- Data retention: yes — we can include a configuration flag in the MAP that sets pilot data to auto-purge at 30 days. I updated the MAP spreadsheet (QP_MAP_v1.xlsx) to reflect that option and the responsible party (QuickPulse -> data ops; Redwood -> storage lifecycle).
- Failure modes that pause the pilot: reproducible PII leakage, critical model hallucination that affects a safety label, and sustained infra instability (>5% error rate for 1 hour). I added those to the exit gates section.
- SOC2 artifacts: those live in our compliance pack; I attached a checklist and will provide the SOC2 report redacted for shared review. SLA_draft_QP.pdf includes the proposed uptime & response targets but not the SOC2 docs — we’ll deliver those under the compliance link.

Next steps I recommend:
- Please nominate one primary acceptance signatory (name + title) from QuickPulse. Procurement copy (procure@quickpulse.ai) is on this thread.
- Karthik and I will host a 30-minute technical kickoff on Friday to align on test harnesses; can you confirm availability?

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.inference.com>

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.inference.com>
Date: 2026-10-21T16:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: QuickPulse MAP: success metrics, exit gates, acceptance tests

Lena / team — adding the technical acceptance checklist here so everyone has a single place to reference. I attached a working copy of acceptance-tests.md to the MAP. Highlights:

- Replay harness: replay 10k records in batches of 500; check label concordance and latency metrics after each batch. Pass = concordance >= 0.84 AND no tail latency > 1s for more than 1% of requests.
- Canary traffic: route 5% of live traffic to pilot model for a 24-hour window; monitor error rate and drift. Pass = error rate < 1% and drift < 2% measured by our drift detector heuristic.
- Stability soak: 72-hour soak with sustained 30 req/min target; pass requires no critical restarts and CPU/GPU utilization remaining within 85% of observed baseline.
- Security checks: validation of purge lifecycle (demo of automated deletion), API token lifecycle validation, and evidence that masked PII is never materialized in logs.

Owners: Redwood (infra/setup/test harness) = Karthik; QuickPulse (data handoff / labeling / final sign-off) = Lena + Samir; Exec review = QuickPulse CTO + Redwood account lead (Priyom / Marissa).

Scheduling note: I propose Friday 10/23 10:00–10:30 PT for the technical kickoff. If that works, I’ll send an invite and a short runbook for the first runs.
